from itertools import combinations
from math import comb, sqrt
from scipy import stats

# === Null A: LoRA-only (3 seeds) vs λ=0.1 (3 seeds) ===
null_a = [56.5, 52.5, 55.0]
treat = [58.0, 58.5, 54.5]
pool_a = null_a + treat
k = 3
obs = sum(treat)/k
mu_a = sum(pool_a)/len(pool_a)
dev_a = abs(obs - mu_a)
ge_a = tw_a = 0
for c in combinations(pool_a, k):
    m = sum(c)/k
    if m >= obs: ge_a += 1
    if abs(m - mu_a) >= dev_a - 1e-12: tw_a += 1
n_a = comb(len(pool_a), k)
print(f"Null A: p_one={ge_a/n_a:.3f}, p_two={tw_a/n_a:.3f}, n_combos={n_a}")
print(f"  obs_mean={obs:.2f}, pool_mean={mu_a:.4f}, dev={dev_a:.4f}")
print(f"  ge={ge_a}, tw={tw_a}")

# === Null B: LoRA + λ=0.005 (6 seeds) vs λ=0.1 (3 seeds) ===
null_b = [56.5, 52.5, 55.0, 57.0, 54.0, 52.5]
pool_b = null_b + treat
obs_b = sum(treat)/k
mu_b = sum(pool_b)/len(pool_b)
dev_b = abs(obs_b - mu_b)
ge_b = tw_b = 0
for c in combinations(pool_b, k):
    m = sum(c)/k
    if m >= obs_b: ge_b += 1
    if abs(m - mu_b) >= dev_b - 1e-12: tw_b += 1
n_b = comb(len(pool_b), k)
print(f"\nNull B: p_one={ge_b/n_b:.3f}, p_two={tw_b/n_b:.3f}, n_combos={n_b}")

# === λ=0.01 exact permutation p-value ===
lora_only = [56.5, 52.5, 55.0]
lam001 = [57.0, 57.5, 54.5]
pool_01 = lora_only + lam001
obs_01 = sum(lam001)/k
mu_01 = sum(pool_01)/len(pool_01)
dev_01 = abs(obs_01 - mu_01)
ge_01 = tw_01 = 0
for c in combinations(pool_01, k):
    m = sum(c)/k
    if m >= obs_01: ge_01 += 1
    if abs(m - mu_01) >= dev_01 - 1e-12: tw_01 += 1
n_01 = comb(len(pool_01), k)
print(f"\nλ=0.01 vs LoRA-only (Null A): p_one={ge_01/n_01:.3f}, p_two={tw_01/n_01:.3f}, n_combos={n_01}")
print(f"  obs_mean={obs_01:.4f}, pool_mean={mu_01:.4f}")

# === Power Analysis ===
# n=3 per group, σ≈2.0pp, α=0.05 one-tailed
# MDE at 80% power using t-test approximation
n_per = 3
sigma = 2.0
alpha = 0.05
df = 2 * n_per - 2  # df=4
t_crit = stats.t.ppf(1 - alpha, df)
t_power = stats.t.ppf(0.80, df)  # for 80% power
# MDE = (t_crit + t_power) * sigma * sqrt(2/n)
MDE = (t_crit + t_power) * sigma * sqrt(2/n_per)
print(f"\nPower Analysis:")
print(f"  df={df}, t_crit(0.05,{df})={t_crit:.3f}, t_80%({df})={t_power:.3f}")
print(f"  MDE at 80% power = ({t_crit:.3f} + {t_power:.3f}) * {sigma} * sqrt(2/{n_per})")
print(f"  MDE = {MDE:.1f} pp")
print(f"  Observed effect = {obs - sum(null_a)/k:.1f} pp")

# Also compute with two-tailed alpha
t_crit_2 = stats.t.ppf(1 - alpha/2, df)
MDE_2 = (t_crit_2 + t_power) * sigma * sqrt(2/n_per)
print(f"  MDE (two-tailed α=0.05) = {MDE_2:.1f} pp")

# Also: permutation-based power is harder to compute exactly, 
# so t-test approx is standard
print(f"\n  Observed effect (λ=0.1 - LoRA mean): {sum(treat)/k - sum(null_a)/k:.2f} pp")

PYEOF

from itertools import combinations
from math import comb

# λ=0.01 vs Null B (LoRA + λ=0.005, 6 values)
null_b = [56.5, 52.5, 55.0, 57.0, 54.0, 52.5]
lam001 = [57.0, 57.5, 54.5]
pool = null_b + lam001
k = 3
obs = sum(lam001)/k
mu = sum(pool)/len(pool)
dev = abs(obs - mu)
ge = tw = 0
for c in combinations(pool, k):
    m = sum(c)/k
    if m >= obs: ge += 1
    if abs(m - mu) >= dev - 1e-12: tw += 1
n = comb(len(pool), k)
print(f"λ=0.01 vs Null B: p_one={ge/n:.3f}, p_two={tw/n:.3f}, n_combos={n}")
print(f"  obs_mean={obs:.4f}, pool_mean={mu:.4f}")
print(f"  ge={ge}, tw={tw}")

# Also enumerate for Null A to confirm
null_a = [56.5, 52.5, 55.0]
pool_a = null_a + lam001
obs_a = sum(lam001)/k
mu_a = sum(pool_a)/len(pool_a)
dev_a = abs(obs_a - mu_a)
ge_a = tw_a = 0
for c in combinations(pool_a, k):
    m = sum(c)/k
    if m >= obs_a: ge_a += 1
    if abs(m - mu_a) >= dev_a - 1e-12: tw_a += 1
n_a = comb(len(pool_a), k)
print(f"\nλ=0.01 vs Null A: p_one={ge_a/n_a:.3f}, p_two={tw_a/n_a:.3f}, n_combos={n_a}")

# Enumerate all combos for Null A to double-check
print("\nAll C(6,3) combos for λ=0.01 Null A test:")
for c in combinations(pool_a, k):
    m = sum(c)/k
    flag_ge = " >= obs" if m >= obs_a else ""
    flag_tw = " |dev|>=" if abs(m - mu_a) >= dev_a - 1e-12 else ""
    print(f"  {c} -> mean={m:.4f}{flag_ge}{flag_tw}")

PYEOF

the marginal signal observed at $n = 2$ dissolves into seed-to-seed variance.

\paragraph{Alternative null construction (Null~A).}
If only the three LoRA-only seeds are used as the null pool ($\{56.5, 52.5, 55.0\}$), we obtain $\binom{6}{3} = 20$ permutations for each comparison. For $\lambda = 0.1$ (treatment mean 57.00\%): one-tailed $p = 3/20 = 0.150$, two-tailed $p = 6/20 = 0.300$. For $\lambda = 0.01$ (treatment mean 56.33\%): one-tailed $p = 4/20 = 0.200$, two-tailed $p = 8/20 = 0.400$. Under the broader Null~B pool, $\lambda = 0.01$ yields one-tailed $p = 10/84 \approx 0.119$, two-tailed $p = 22/84 \approx 0.262$. All tests are non-significant at $\alpha = 0.05$; the narrower Null~A yields \emph{larger} $p$-values because the LoRA-only pool already contains a high seed (56.5\%), making the treatment means less extreme by comparison.

A Phase~2 ablation reinforces this conclusion.
